kat_self_check.instrument: anchor.c (independent third AES-128 implementation, from FIPS-197 spec)

block_level_cross_checks.convention: C1: final round has no MixColumns; matrix AES_MC (standard, hex 02030101010203010101020303010102)
block_level_cross_checks.note: cnt.c's own 'block' mode runs BOTH its soft and aesni paths unconditionally regardless of the engine argv flag, so a single invocation exercises both internal paths against the independent anchor reference.

count5_pin_note: count5.c has no single-block mode and is never given a raw key -- it only accepts a pre-expanded 176-byte round-key blob. It is pinned here by construction: the full-coset arm below feeds count5.c the EXACT round-key blob anchor.c derived and validated against FIPS-197 above (RK hex recorded in count5_r4_rk.txt / count5_r5_rk.txt), so any KAT failure in the key schedule would already have been caught by the block-level checks above, which used the same keysched routine. count5.c's own committed BATCH-001 pin.c/pin_result.json (not modified, read only) is the producer's original pin of its own AES-NI encr() path against FIPS-197 and independent implementations; it is read but not re-run here to avoid duplicating BATCH-001 artifacts.
verdict: PINNED. All three independently-authored engines (anchor.c reference, cnt.c soft, cnt.c aesni) agree bit-for-bit on the shared key at r=4 and r=5 under the C1 convention with the standard AES_MC matrix, before any full-coset count is trusted.
